candidate_datasets.name: NIST Statistical Test Suite
candidate_datasets.role: public randomness tests

candidate_datasets.name: TestU01
candidate_datasets.role: public generator-testing suite

obstacles: Amenability to analysis has no objective scale.
Every deterministic finite generator has some mathematical description.
Failure to detect deviation is not perfect randomness.
assessments.rationale: A selected generator corpus can test a proxy correlation, but the proposed implication is vague and selection-sensitive. Existing tests cannot establish the absence of all deviations, so only restricted versions are resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Define production rate as entropy rate per active component and classify mechanisms using interventions that hold initial state fixed while shielding or varying environmental inputs. Across a representative sample, test whether high-rate systems overwhelmingly show repeatable deterministic internal generation.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public repeated-run experimental data for selected systems

candidate_datasets.name: Zenodo
candidate_datasets.role: public repository for selected physical and engineered random-system records

obstacles: Existing observations rarely isolate all three mechanisms.
System boundaries determine what counts as intrinsic.
No representative dataset spans natural and engineered systems.
assessments.rationale: The claimed mechanism-frequency relationship is testable in principle with controlled repeated experiments. Public data are piecemeal and lack the interventions and population coverage required for the stated generality.

assessments.operationalization: Use repeated runs with measured and tightly controlled initial conditions, align trajectories, and quantify exact or local-pattern reproducibility as perturbation size is varied. Compare with runs receiving controlled environmental noise and with deliberately varied initial states.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public repeated-run experimental datasets for selected systems

candidate_datasets.name: Zenodo
candidate_datasets.role: public experimental datasets and simulation records

obstacles: Microscopic state cannot usually be reset exactly.
Unmeasured environmental inputs can mimic intrinsic sensitivity.
Deterministic chaos can make intrinsic dynamics nonrepeatable after tiny perturbations.
assessments.rationale: Controlled repeated-run datasets can test selected systems and compare mechanism predictions. Existing public data seldom measure perturbations finely enough, and repeatability is not uniquely diagnostic of intrinsic randomness generation.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify within-organism bilateral similarity and within-species recurrence of fine-scale pattern features, then compare likelihoods under shared developmental noise, environmental noise, and deterministic instability models. A reproducible excess uniquely predicted by deterministic intrinsic generation would support the claim; successful stochastic alternatives would refute its necessity.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public organismal image and morphology records for measuring bilateral and within-species pattern similarity

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: large public image collection spanning many patterned species

obstacles: Intrinsic and stochastic developmental mechanisms can produce the same pattern statistics.
The universal necessity language spans poorly sampled physical and biological systems.
assessments.rationale: Similarity and apparent randomness require substantial choices of features and null models. Public images permit restricted comparative tests, but they rarely include developmental histories or controlled environmental and initial-condition variation. Observational similarity alone cannot establish that intrinsic deterministic randomness is the only possible source.

assessments.operationalization: Simulate discrete growth and transport models with matched noise amplitudes supplied externally, pseudorandomly, or by deterministic chaotic rules, and measure anisotropy and interface roughness after coarse-graining. Convergence to the same smooth macroscopic observables would support mechanism-independence, while systematic source-dependent differences would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Wolfram Atlas of Simple Programs
candidate_datasets.role: public rules and generated behavior for cellular-automaton comparisons

obstacles: Smoothness, large scale, and mainly are model-dependent.
A finite model survey cannot establish the assertion for all discrete systems.
assessments.rationale: The computational examples can be reproduced and extended with standard simulation. Noise-source interventions have useful discriminating power for specified model classes. The broad extension to fluids and the assertion that averaging is the main cause remain only partially covered.

assessments.operationalization: For a defined ensemble of discrete stochastic systems, estimate microscopic decorrelation, macroscopic feature, and growth timescales and test whether smooth coarse-grained trajectories occur only when the first is much shorter. Any robust counterexample with continuous macroscopic behavior but no timescale separation would refute the necessity claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Wolfram Atlas of Simple Programs
candidate_datasets.role: public computational systems that can be simulated and classified by timescale separation

obstacles: Continuous behavior and relevant feature lack unique definitions.
The claim ranges over an unbounded class of systems.
assessments.rationale: Timescale ratios and coarse-grained smoothness are measurable once a model ensemble and observables are fixed. Existing software supports broad computational searches, but no finite enumeration resolves an unrestricted only-when principle. Results can therefore test substantial restricted classes, not the full scope.

assessments.operationalization: Enumerate specified one-, two-, and higher-dimensional binary cellular-automaton rule classes, initialize each over densities bracketing one half, and classify whether the majority color reaches consensus as size and time increase. Compare the fraction of qualifying rules by dimension and test boundary pinning as a mediator.

candidate_datasets.name: Wolfram Atlas of Simple Programs
candidate_datasets.role: rule definitions and behavior for one-dimensional cellular automata

obstacles: Increasingly common depends strongly on the sampled rule family and neighborhood.
Finite simulations can confuse very long transients with stuck boundaries.
assessments.rationale: The transition and takeover behavior have direct computational criteria. Elementary and other bounded rule spaces can be exhaustively or systematically sampled using public software. The unrestricted comparison across all dimensions and rule parameterizations prevents a fully general resolution.

assessments.operationalization: Compile continuous dynamical models and measured natural systems, identify attractors and transition states, and estimate how often a small discrete state model predicts held-out trajectories as well as continuous alternatives. Frequent finite-state dynamics and superior predictive performance would support the claim; prevalent irreducibly continuous observables would oppose it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public curated dynamical models, including biochemical reaction systems with continuous kinetics

obstacles: Appropriate is a purpose-dependent modelling judgment.
Published model repositories are not representative samples of natural systems.
assessments.rationale: Multistability and discrete transitions can be measured in continuous models, but commonness and model appropriateness require sampling and task definitions not supplied by the claim. BioModels supports a restricted survey. Predictive equivalence also does not establish that a discrete model is uniquely most appropriate.

assessments.operationalization: Define a representative census of complex natural phenomena and formal competing generative models based on equilibrium constraints versus explicit dynamics, then compare out-of-sample likelihood and computational cost. The claim would be supported if constraint models almost never provide the best account and their required search exceeds physically available computation.
obstacles: No representative dataset links natural phenomena to adjudicated explanatory mechanisms.
Best explained and complex are not uniquely operationalized.
Model fit cannot by itself establish the historical causal process.
assessments.rationale: Restricted cases can be studied, but the near-universal statement requires a representative inventory that does not exist. Its explanatory and computational language admits competing operationalizations. New comparative measurements and mechanistic records would be needed even after formalizing the terms.

assessments.operationalization: Benchmark greedy descent, randomized local search, annealing, and modern solvers over preregistered ensembles of discrete constraint problems, measuring local-minimum trapping, residual violations, and scaling. Broadly persistent trapping and absence of a cross-class speedup would support the computational portion; efficient broad solvers or smooth landscapes would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: SAT Competition
candidate_datasets.role: public benchmark instances and solver results for discrete constraint satisfaction

obstacles: Almost always and broad classes depend on the benchmark distribution.
Failure of tested algorithms cannot prove that no general speed-up works.
The inference to natural systems needs independent mechanistic data.
assessments.rationale: Algorithmic trapping is measurable on public benchmarks and simulations. Such tests discriminate the performance claims for defined instance families. They cannot establish impossibility across broad classes or the final generalization about how closely natural systems satisfy constraints.

assessments.operationalization: For public experimental and simulated packing trajectories, compare final packing fraction and crystalline order after compression or agitation of monodisperse disks and spheres against the known densest values. Frequent spontaneous attainment in spheres would refute the claim; robust jamming below crystalline order across protocols would support it.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public repository containing experimental datasets from granular packing studies

obstacles: Results depend strongly on friction, container geometry, polydispersity, and agitation protocol.
Essentially never cannot be established from finite trials.
Careful one-by-one placement is not a sharply bounded intervention.
assessments.rationale: Packing density and order are standard observables, and existing experiments and simulations cover many protocols. Public records are scattered and do not uniformly span the claim's protocol space. They can resolve typical behavior under defined conditions but not the absolute or almost-always wording.

assessments.operationalization: Classify biological forms by quantified structural complexity and reconstruct whether each trait arose chiefly through selection on a functional constraint or through developmental growth dynamics. The claim predicts that selection-dominated constraint solutions occupy only the low-complexity range, whereas complex forms trace to explicit developmental rules.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: public morphological matrices and images for restricted comparative trait analyses

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public phylogenetic synthesis for comparative analyses

obstacles: Constraint satisfaction, growth-rule causation, and form complexity are difficult to separate.
Existing comparative data rarely identify the causal contribution of selection versus development.
The dichotomy is not exhaustive.
assessments.rationale: Morphology and phylogeny data exist, but the central causal attribution is generally absent. Retrospective associations cannot cleanly distinguish selection from developmental mechanisms because both jointly shape traits. assessments.operationalization: Choose explicit rule-description and spacetime-behavior complexity measures, enumerate bounded simple-program families, and estimate their association while examining minimally differing rule pairs. Counterexamples in both directions and weak correspondence would support the claim; a robust monotone mapping would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Wolfram Atlas of Simple Programs
candidate_datasets.role: public exhaustive rule tables and generated patterns for simple program families

obstacles: Complexity has several inequivalent measures.
The extension from formal programs to natural systems is not resolved by enumeration.
assessments.rationale: For specified simple-program families the rules and outputs are fully available and standard computations can test direct correspondence. assessments.operationalization: Identify nested natural patterns with time-resolved formation data and classify their mechanism as top-down splitting or bottom-up aggregation using lineage or material tracking. A representative majority produced by aggregation would support the frequency claim.

candidate_datasets.name: PANGAEA
candidate_datasets.role: public earth and environmental datasets that may support restricted studies of nested natural patterns

obstacles: No representative census of nested patterns and formation mechanisms exists.
Final geometry often cannot identify whether splitting or aggregation produced it.
More common lacks a defined reference population.
assessments.rationale: The two mechanism classes can be defined in particular systems, but static pattern repositories do not contain the needed developmental histories. Existing data are highly domain-specific and not adequate for a statement about nature generally. Broad resolution requires new time-resolved mechanistic observations.

assessments.operationalization: Simulate a preregistered ensemble of coarsening systems with independently growing domains, including random-walk boundaries, and quantify hierarchical nesting in merger trees. A system satisfying the premises but consistently lacking nested merger structure would refute the generic assertion.

candidate_datasets.name: Wolfram Atlas of Simple Programs
candidate_datasets.role: public cellular-automaton rules and outputs for relevant computational examples

obstacles: Essentially any system is an unbounded universal claim.
Nested resemblance needs a quantitative threshold.
Finite runs may miss asymptotic coarsening behavior.
assessments.rationale: Domain mergers naturally generate explicit trees whose nesting can be measured in simulation. Public rules and software permit broad tests including the named cellular automata. Finite model ensembles cannot settle the unrestricted universality wording.

assessments.operationalization: The statement could be reframed as a comparison of how well human visual ratings and numerical summaries predict held-out model failures, but that would test a chosen evaluation workflow rather than the asserted normative best first step.
obstacles: Best first test is normative and task-dependent.
Overall picture and adequate assessment have no invariant decision criteria.
assessments.rationale: The claim recommends a modelling practice rather than specifying a measurable consequence. Empirical studies of evaluator performance would depend on chosen tasks, losses, and observers and could not establish visual comparison as generally best. Operationalization would materially reinterpret the statement.

assessments.operationalization: Compare preregistered geometric descriptors of time-resolved snow-crystal images with outputs from the exact hexagonal rule and rival diffusion and heat-transport models. Support requires reproduction of the main descriptors plus an observed relation between local latent-heat conditions and growth suppression; visual similarity alone is insufficient.
obstacles: Archival final images lack local temperature and vapor histories.
Many distinct growth mechanisms can produce similar hexagonal morphology.
Main features is underspecified.
assessments.rationale: The cellular automaton is straightforward to simulate and snow-crystal images permit morphology comparison. Existing public imagery is less suitable for testing the proposed latent-heat mechanism, and shape fit has limited discrimination among rival crystal-growth models. assessments.operationalization: Segment time-lapse images of individual snowflakes, classify each frame by branchiness and faceting, and test for repeated ordered transitions associated with branch collisions. Persistent monotonic morphology or transitions unrelated to collisions would refute the prediction.
obstacles: Public collections emphasize final crystals rather than complete growth trajectories.
Temperature and supersaturation changes can independently drive morphology transitions.
assessments.rationale: The prediction maps cleanly to time-resolved shape measurements and collision events. However, broad open datasets of individual snowflakes throughout growth with controlled conditions are not readily available. New controlled time-lapse observations are needed for a decisive test.

assessments.operationalization: Use repeated crystal-growth trajectories with measured seed and environmental perturbations to fit deterministic instability and exogenous-noise models, then compare held-out path distributions and repeatability. candidate_datasets.name: PANGAEA
candidate_datasets.role: public repository for restricted crystal-growth and environmental records

obstacles: Unmeasured microscopic seed defects can masquerade as intrinsic randomness.
Often spans an undefined population of crystalline materials.
Model non-identifiability limits causal attribution.
assessments.rationale: Crystal shapes can be quantified, but assigning randomness to intrinsic dynamics requires unusually complete initial-condition and environmental measurements. Existing public records permit only selected case studies. Even close deterministic fits may not discriminate chaos from amplified unobserved noise.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze crack trajectories and displacement fields in specimens with independently mapped heterogeneity, comparing deterministic fracture models with heterogeneity-driven models across material classes and scales. A material-independent residual roughness law predicted by the interaction model would support the claim; strong dependence on mapped disorder would oppose it.

candidate_datasets.name: Materials Data Facility
candidate_datasets.role: public materials datasets potentially containing fracture images and mechanical measurements

obstacles: Microscopic material disorder is difficult to measure completely before fracture.

Coverage from crystals to geological faults is inadequate.
assessments.rationale: Fracture roughness and displacement fields are standard observables, and some public datasets exist. The broad material-independence and causal exclusion of irregularities are much harder to test than roughness itself. Current data support restricted comparisons but not the full scope.

assessments.operationalization: Simulate particle systems that vary microscopic rules while preserving or breaking specified conservation laws and measure convergence of coarse-grained fields to hydrodynamic equations and benchmark flows. candidate_datasets.name: NIST Chemistry WebBook
candidate_datasets.role: public thermophysical reference data for comparing macroscopic fluid properties

candidate_datasets.name: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Databases

assessments.operationalization: For ensembles of nearly identical initial flow fields, track divergence of low-wavenumber velocity and pressure observables while varying viscosity and flow regime. candidate_datasets.name: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Databases
candidate_datasets.role: public high-resolution turbulent flow fields for perturbation and scale-dependent divergence analyses

obstacles: Single trajectories do not provide controlled pairs of nearby initial conditions.
Almost all cases lacks a sampling distribution over flows.
Large scale and discernible require chosen filters and tolerances.

assessments.operationalization: Compare turbulence statistics in repeated flows with controlled macroscopic forcing while varying external disturbances and molecular noise in matched simulations. The claim is supported if large-scale dynamics generate nearly invariant turbulent statistics after those inputs are suppressed or varied, but refuted if output randomness tracks them.

candidate_datasets.name: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Databases
candidate_datasets.role: public direct numerical simulation fields for multiscale turbulence analysis

obstacles: Chaotic amplification makes internally generated and unmeasured input randomness observationally similar.
Most existing datasets do not independently vary molecular noise.
Mostly needs a variance attribution convention.
assessments.rationale: Existing turbulence simulations permit counterfactual perturbations and scale-resolved energy analyses. They cover canonical flows and can test whether large-scale dynamics sustain randomness. Causal attribution among forcing noise, initial uncertainty, and intrinsic instability remains confounded in observational records.

assessments.operationalization: Repeat a turbulent-flow experiment from independently reset initial conditions, quantify apparent randomness using preregistered statistics, and measure spatial-temporal similarity across runs. Random-looking patterns with reproducibility far above a stochastic-input baseline support the prediction; ordinary run-to-run divergence refutes it.
obstacles: Existing turbulence archives rarely contain independently repeated, meticulously reset runs.
Effective repeatability needs spatial, temporal, and tolerance definitions.
Residual preparation differences may dominate chaotic divergence.
assessments.rationale: The prediction admits a clean repeated-experiment test with strong discriminating power. Public databases predominantly provide single experiments or simulations, not the required replicated physical runs under carefully matched conditions. New laboratory data are therefore needed.

assessments.operationalization: For traits with measurable fitness landscapes, compare observed phenotypes with global optima and simulate evolutionary search under reconstructed mutation, population, and generation counts. Widespread optimality on demonstrably complex landscapes would refute the claim; persistent suboptimality would support only restricted versions.

candidate_datasets.name: ProteinGym
candidate_datasets.role: public deep-mutational-scanning benchmarks for empirical local fitness landscapes

obstacles: Global biological fitness is environment-dependent and multidimensional.
Available fitness landscapes cover tiny molecular subsets and few generations.
Present suboptimality does not identify search-time insufficiency as its cause.
assessments.rationale: Empirical fitness landscapes can test optimization claims for proteins and laboratory systems. They do not span organismal features, deep time, or the full adaptive history, and complexity lacks one accepted metric. Existing data therefore resolve proxies and restricted cases only.

assessments.operationalization: Define organismal complexity features, map each to a developmental program, and estimate causal variance attributable to neutral program-output prevalence versus adaptive selection using phylogenetic and fitness data. A dominant neutral-program contribution across a representative feature sample would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public phylogenetic framework for restricted comparative tests

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: public morphological matrices for sampling organismal features

obstacles: Randomly chosen programs has no natural sampling distribution.
Adaptation and developmental generation are not mutually exclusive causes.
No dataset assigns causal origins to a representative share of biological complexity.
assessments.rationale: Existing morphology and phylogeny resources provide outcomes but not the required causal partition. The central reference distribution over programs is undefined, substantially lowering operationalizability. Major new developmental and fitness data would still leave difficult causal-identification assumptions.

assessments.operationalization: Apply preregistered morphological-complexity measures to homologous organismal parts in fossil and extant specimens, model measurement and preservation bias, and estimate temporal trends over several hundred million years. A substantial sustained increase across measures would refute constancy.

candidate_datasets.name: Paleobiology Database
candidate_datasets.role: public fossil occurrence and taxonomic data for temporal sampling

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: public morphological matrices and media for comparative measurements

assessments.operationalization: Identify cis-regulatory and coding loci causally required for shell pigmentation through expression, perturbation, and segregation evidence, then measure the minimal sequence and regulatory-network description sufficient to recreate pattern classes. candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Gene
candidate_datasets.role: public gene records and linked sequence and functional evidence for pigmentation genes

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Sequence Read Archive

Sequence association does not identify the complete causal program.
Functional genomic coverage of shell-pattern diversity is sparse.
assessments.rationale: Public mollusc genomes and transcriptomes can identify candidate pigmentation components in some species. assessments.operationalization: Across traits with mapped genotype-phenotype-fitness relations, quantify behavioral complexity and the response to selection, then test whether selection response approaches zero above a preregistered complexity threshold. candidate_datasets.name: ProteinGym
candidate_datasets.role: public empirical fitness landscapes for restricted tests of selection and sequence-function complexity

Selection response is confounded by mutation supply, population size, and environment.

assessments.operationalization: Compare trait complexity, modular independence, and smooth parameter sensitivity before and after known episodes or experiments of strong selection, controlling for drift and developmental constraint. candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public evolutionary and experimental datasets for restricted selection studies

obstacles: Engineering-like and complexity are multidimensional judgments.
Historical selection intensity is rarely observed directly.
Developmental constraints can mimic selection for modularity.

assessments.operationalization: Across related species, estimate phylogenetic rates for homologous traits, assign quantitative pattern-complexity scores, and test their association while separately estimating evidence of stabilizing or directional selection. The claim predicts a near-universal positive rate-complexity relationship and low rates for selected features.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: public morphological matrices and images for cross-species trait comparisons

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public phylogenies for estimating trait-change rates

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: public organism images for pigmentation and texture measurements

obstacles: Obvious complexity is observer- and metric-dependent.

Rapid change can itself be driven by selection.

assessments.operationalization: For independently evolved structures, estimate their frequency under an explicit distribution of developmental programs and measure fitness effects in each lineage. candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public phylogenetic synthesis for identifying independent origins

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: public morphological data for cataloguing convergent structures

obstacles: There is no agreed probability distribution over possible developmental programs.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate long-term trends in multiple organismal complexity measures from fossil phylogenies and compare trait gains and losses with evidence of selection. candidate_datasets.name: Paleobiology Database
candidate_datasets.role: public fossil occurrences for long-term diversity and trait sampling

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: public morphological character matrices

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: public phylogenetic framework for trait-gain and loss analyses

obstacles: Complexity has no single accepted measure.

assessments.operationalization: Fit recursive fixed-angle, fixed-ratio branching models to time-resolved and mature plant architectures across major lineages, then compare held-out geometry with models allowing nonrecursive developmental control and environmental plasticity. candidate_datasets.name: TRY Plant Trait Database
candidate_datasets.role: plant trait resource for restricted comparative analyses

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public three-dimensional morphology records that may include branching architectures

assessments.rationale: Plant architecture and recursive-model parameters are measurable, and existing repositories cover some taxa. assessments.operationalization: Fit one explicitly shared branching-growth model to whole-plant architectures and leaf-development trajectories, perturb its parameters, and test whether it predicts observed leaf-shape transitions. candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public morphology records for plant and leaf shape comparisons

Time-resolved leaf development and whole-plant architecture are rarely paired.

Existing public datasets are not designed to connect both scales within the same genotypes and developmental trajectories. Restricted shape predictions are testable, but the shared causal process is not decisively resolved.

assessments.operationalization: Measure successive organ angles and inhibitory-field markers in shoot apical meristems, perturb the relevant transport or signaling process, and compare trajectories with the specified depletion model and optimization alternatives. Recovery of approximately 137.5 degrees from measured dynamics and predicted perturbation responses would support the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: BioStudies
candidate_datasets.role: public biological study data, including plant imaging and perturbation supplements

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public expression data relevant to meristem patterning pathways

obstacles: The chemical concentration in the claim is not uniquely specified.

assessments.rationale: Phyllotactic angles and molecular perturbations are measurable, and public studies can test portions of the inhibitory mechanism. Existing data are scattered and do not cover the claimed universality. Similar predictions from rival models reduce causal discrimination.

assessments.operationalization: Generate the morphology space of the stated few-parameter shell-growth model, embed standardized three-dimensional scans of mollusc shells in the same shape descriptors, and estimate coverage in both directions. candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public three-dimensional mollusc shell models for geometric comparison

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: public occurrence and specimen-linked records for assessing taxonomic shell coverage

obstacles: Essentially every form needs a coverage threshold and sampling measure over parameter space.
Museum scans are taxonomically and morphologically biased.
Shape agreement does not establish secretion-rate causation.
assessments.rationale: The model can be exhaustively sampled and public shell scans permit direct geometric tests. assessments.operationalization: Track lineage, spatial domain size, morphogen gradients, and regulatory state in embryo atlases to test whether fate domains recursively subdivide near a fixed length scale and whether proximal regions consistently precede distal subregions. candidate_datasets.name: EMBL-EBI Single Cell Expression Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: public developmental single-cell expression datasets across organisms

candidate_datasets.name: BioStudies
candidate_datasets.role: public imaging and supplementary developmental datasets

obstacles: Single-cell atlases often lack continuous spatial and lineage information.
Developmental length scales vary among tissues, stages, and species.
Hierarchical description does not isolate fixed scale as the cause.
assessments.rationale: Modern developmental atlases contain regulatory states and sometimes spatial trajectories suitable for selected embryos. assessments.operationalization: Register three-dimensional shapes of related animals, fit low-dimensional smooth deformation fields, and compare inferred regional scaling with measured developmental growth rates. assessments.operationalization: Measure accuracy and response time for matched repetitive and recursively nested patterns while controlling uniform-area size, then compare human performance with pointer-based compression scores. A large selective human deficit for nesting supports the claim.
